title: AstraZeneca bulks up MASH, cardio work in up to $1.5B AI partnership with insitro
snippet: AstraZeneca will tap AI-focused insitro to find new targets for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and cardiomyopathies, following the Phase 3 failure of its Ionis-partnered Wainua in transthyretin-mediated amyloid cardiomyopathy.

title: Webinar: The China question: Can US biotechs lead as investment heads east?
snippet: In this webinar, BioSpace will gathered experts to discuss China’s impact on the future of biotech and how both U.S. and Chinese companies can thrive—and maybe even collaborate.

title: GSK laying off 1.2K+ in Belgium
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: FDA's latest rare disease framework seeks to prioritize consistency in flexibility
snippet: Following several recent initiatives, the FDA's newest rare disease framework sets out to standardize the agency's approach to scientific evidence and bring rare disease therapies to patients faster.

title: Stoffels strikes up new biotech in return to Galapagos cell therapy mission
snippet: A new biotech co-founded by Paul Stoffels has formed to take on the CAR T cell assets of Galapagos almost a year after the company—now known as Lakefront Biotherapeutics—abandoned them.

title: Arrowhead’s blood-brain barrier tech is ‘arguably better’ than others, analysts say after data drop
snippet: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals’ siRNA candidate achieved “compelling” tau reductions in an early study of healthy volunteers, with a magnitude of effect that seems to outperformother blood-brain barrier platforms, according to Stifel.

title: Vanda freezes Novartis-originated social anxiety program after late-stage disappointment
snippet: While Oppenheimer doesn’t see the Phase 3 stumble of VQW-765 as highly detrimental to Vanda Pharmaceuticals, the analyst nevertheless believes the stakes are now higher for the company’s planned Q4 readout for Nereus in GLP-1-induced vomiting.

title: The decisions behind scientific progress
snippet: In this episode of Denatured, presented by Cytiva, Jennifer Smith-Parker speaks to Nicolas Pivet, VP & GM, Manufacturing & Digital Solutions at Cytiva. In this episode, we explore how biopharma’s real bottleneck isn’t too little data—it’s too little confidence in the decisions that drive development, manufacturing and...

title: Gilead snags equity stake in Vir with up to $1.87B deal for three T cell engagers
snippet: The Gilead Sciences deal, which include $135 million in upfront and near-term payments, marks a critical platform validation for Vir Biotechnology as investors await an upcoming readout in solid tumors.

title: Verastem reports ‘robust’ response rate in pancreatic cancer subgroup where Rasonque struggled
snippet: Revolution Medicines’ recently approved drug showed a 24% overall response rate and a high rate of side effects in patients whose cancer has a G12D mutation, reinforcing Mizuho’s view that a more specific agent such as Verastem Oncology’s VS-7375 “should come first for G12D patients.”

title: ‘Pharma bro’ Shkreli runs afoul of court’s lifetime pharma ban
snippet: Since his release from prison in 2022, Martin Shkreli has traded stocks and publicly opined on news events, damaging reputations and sinking share prices for small biotechs including Capricor and Cassava, the FTC alleges.

title: GSK plans 1.2K+ layoffs at Belgium sites as $2.5B restructure gains momentum
snippet: The layoffs across GSK’s Belgium sites come on the heels of the pharma’s planned shuttering of its German vaccine manufacturing site, which prompted job cuts for about 650 employees.

title: Zealand pens up to $1.2B deal with Generate for AI-designed obesity, metabolic drugs
snippet: Obesity-focused Zealand Pharma is buying into Generate:Biomedicines’s generative AI platform to create new multispecific drug candidates.

title: Verdiva ends mid-stage study of oral GLP-1 amid ‘market evolution’
snippet: The candidate is an oral version of ecnoglutide, a subcutaneous formulation of which is approved in China for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Pfizer owns commercialization rights for ecnoglutide in the Asian country.

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Alnylam bulls and bears fight it out after business-shaking guidance cut
snippet: While Alnylam’s recent reduced revenue guidance spooked investors, analysts remain broadly bullish on the biotech’s commercial prospects.

title: J&J’s disappointing Q3, RevMed’s subgroup data, BMS’ ‘mixed’ results, Caribou’s cutback
snippet: Johnson & Johnson beat analyst expectations in the third quarter but left Wall Street wanting more; BMS dominated the news cycle on Monday with a Phase 3 win validating its $4.1 billion RayzeBio buy and mixed data in a late-stage pulmonary fibrosis trial; Revolution Medicines’ newly approved pancreatic cancer drug wor...

title: European biotech leaders split on US-China fight for deal dominance, survey finds
snippet: While industry leaders are unsure whether the U.S. or China will prevail, they are largely united in the belief that Europe is lagging behind.

title: Jazz CEO calls on industry to help rebuild momentum for leadership diversity
snippet: The first-time CEO says her own sponsors took chances on her—and that industry leaders need to do the same to rebuild momentum for gender equity.

title: J&J’s innovative medicines carried Q3 as medtech disappoints, but newer medicines absent
snippet: While innovative medicine supported Johnson & Johnson’s “in line” earnings for the third quarter of 2026, investors were disappointed to see older medicines carrying the bag.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
